text:
Edmonton scored four times on 17 shots and walked out of Crypto.com Arena with a win the numbers say belonged to Los Angeles. The Kings held a 40-17 edge in shots on goal and a 80-37 edge in shot attempts, and the quality of their chances (2.94 expected goals to 2.19) put them on the winning side in 72 percent of simulated replays. Devon Levi stopped 39 of 40 and saved nearly two goals more than the chances against him should have allowed.

The game was effectively settled in the first period. Leon Draisaitl opened the scoring at 7:16 on a snap shot with only an 8 percent chance of going in, and Vasily Podkolzin converted a power play snap shot 60 seconds later. Connor McDavid added a backhand at 15:48 for a 3-0 lead, and he finished with a goal and three assists. Edmonton generated 0.89 expected goals in that period to Los Angeles's 0.56, which was about as good as the Oilers looked all night. At even strength they managed just 0.88 expected goals to the Kings' 1.79.

Los Angeles took over in the second, outchancing Edmonton 1.66 to 0.34, but the payoff came late. Brandt Clarke, who put six shots on goal, beat Darcy Kuemper's replacement-less counterpart at 17:29 on a 3 percent look to make it 3-1. Kuemper had allowed all three early goals on seven shots, while Anton Forsberg stopped all nine he faced in relief. Podkolzin sealed it at 17:42 of the third with his second goal of the night, a wrist shot that left Edmonton ahead 4-1 and Los Angeles wondering how it lost.
